facts.big: Where do we…? · Is there…? · Are there…?
facts.label: Check-in no camping
facts.sub: Diga I have a reservation. Pergunte Where do we put the tent? Pergunte Is there firewood? e Are there mosquitoes at night? Peça informação: Is there a trail to the lake?

facts.label: Espaços numerados
facts.sub: Os campings dos EUA dividem a área em espaços numerados. Cada espaço tem um lugar plano para a barraca, uma mesa de piquenique e, às vezes, um pequeno anel para fogueira.

facts.label: Regras de fogueira
facts.sub: Faça fogueira somente no anel do seu espaço e nunca deixe o fogo sozinho. Em épocas secas, algumas regiões proíbem fogueiras. O guarda sempre avisa quando há risco.

mini.en: Good idea. Is there a trail to the {lake|river|hill}?

facts.label: Cuidado com a comida
facts.sub: Em áreas com ursos, guarde a comida em caixas de metal ou no carro. Nunca deixe comida na barraca, porque o cheiro atrai animais.

facts.label: Placas de trilha
facts.sub: As trilhas têm placas que mostram a distância e o nível de dificuldade. Leve água, protetor solar e um mapa, e volte antes de escurecer.

compare.br: In Brazil, a camping also has barracas and fogueira, and many people go by car.
compare.tip: Say: “Where do we put the tent?”
compare.us: In the USA, you often reserve a numbered site, and the ranger tells you the fire rules.

pages.title: A fire and a lantern · 1/3
paragraphs: It is four o’clock in the afternoon at a campground in the mountains. The air is cool, and the trees are tall. Ana arrives in a small car with a big backpack. She carries a lantern, a rope and a long pole. A park ranger named Sam waits at the office. Ana is tired, but she is happy.
“Welcome to the campground! Do you have a reservation?” says Sam. “Yes, for two nights. Where do we put the tent?” says Ana. “Put it in site nine, near the trees.” says Sam.

pages.title: A fire and a lantern · 3/3
paragraphs: “Great. Do I need a compass?” says Ana. “No, the trail is easy. Enjoy your trip!” says Sam. Ana walks to site nine and opens the tent. She ties the rope between two trees. That evening, she makes a small fire with the firewood. She roasts marshmallows and watches the sparks. A cool wind comes, and she turns on the lantern. In the tent, she zips the door and falls asleep.
